title: Per-script reviewer qualification criteria and onboarding workflow
context: Every scheme must be reviewed by a qualified per-script reviewer before it is released. A false reversibility claim or an incorrect grapheme mapping is a real harm — a person's name corrupted silently. The qualification criteria and onboarding workflow establish what qualifies someone to review a scheme (native/near-native script command, linguistic/transliteration competence, conflict-of-interest declaration), how reviews are structured, when a second reviewer is mandatory, and how disagreements are resolved. These rules govern all future scheme reviews.
objective: Write docs/reviewers/qualification-criteria.md (or equivalent) defining objective per-script reviewer qualification criteria, the onboarding/sign-off workflow, reviewer independence rules, the mandatory second-reviewer rule, back-mapping QA for strict claims, and the disagreement resolution rule (reconcile against open sources and checker → escalate → more conservative reversibility class wins, recorded in review.yaml).
acceptanceCriteria: Document defines objective criteria for 'qualified per-script reviewer': native or near-native command of the script plus linguistic/transliteration competence for the specific script pair; criteria are concrete and checkable, not vague
Document defines the conflict-of-interest declaration requirement: any reviewer records their COI status; the human who ran the drafting agent may not be the sole sign-off reviewer for that scheme
Document defines when a second independent qualified reviewer is MANDATORY: (a) any scheme claiming strict reversibility, (b) the first scheme in each new script family
Document defines back-mapping QA requirement for strict claims: the second reviewer verifies the inverse direction independently

Document defines the disagreement resolution rule: reconcile against open sources and the checker → escalate to a third reviewer/maintainer → the more conservative reversibility class wins (e.g., strict downgraded to normalized); outcome recorded in review.yaml
Document defines the UNCERTAIN: flag format and the rule that no sign-off may be recorded while any agent flag is unresolved
Document is stored in docs/reviewers/ and linked from CONTRIBUTING.md or PLAN.md
resources: PLAN.md — Quality, review & risk gates section; Governance section
output: docs/reviewers/qualification-criteria.md (or docs/reviewers/README.md) defining qualification, onboarding, independence, second-reviewer, back-mapping QA, and disagreement rules
